text:
raj: quick heads-up — ran an adaptive-quant routing sweep across Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-7B last night. Trying a routing policy that prefers FP8 kernels, falls back to INT8, then to 4-bit. sharing raw trace + config. TL;DR: FP8 wins for latency on our A100 pool but gave a small quality delta on long-context Qwen prompts. want opinions on safe fallback thresholds.

perf-bot: summary results (batch=1/seq=1024 on A100):
```
model     | FP8_path tps | INT8_fallback tps | 4bit tps | avg latency ms | ppl change
Llama-13B | 210 tok/s     | 150 tok/s         | 95 tok/s  | 34ms           | +0.6%
Mistral-7B| 320 tok/s     | 220 tok/s         | 140 tok/s | 21ms           | +0.3%
Qwen-7B   | 180 tok/s     | 130 tok/s         | 90 tok/s  | 48ms           | +1.8%
```

any a note: these are single-request numbers with KV warm cache. cold-KV copies add ~3-6ms on Llama-13B and up to ~10ms on Qwen due to bigger hidden dims.

anya: nice. did you capture kernel-selection logs? curious where we flip to INT8 — is it based on SNR or inference latency overshoot?

raj: logs included. current routing rule: if model_profile.fp8_error_estimate > 0.15 OR recent_tail_latency > latency_slo*1.25 => demote to INT8. then if int8_error_estimate > 0.12 => demote to 4bit (last resort). We estimate error via calibration set drift score (KL on a small held prompt list).

michael: can you paste the config? want to try with our canary hosts (mixed A100 + H100).

raj: config snip below — meant to be lightweight and shareable:
```
{\n  "model_matchers": ["llama*","mistral*","qwen*"],\n  "routing_policy": "prefer_fp8",\n  "fallbacks": [\n    {"to":"int8", "trigger": {"fp8_error_estimate": 0.15, "latency_multiplier": 1.25}},\n    {"to":"4bit","trigger": {"int8_error_estimate": 0.12}}\n  ],\n  "kv_policy": {"warm_prefetch": true, "max_kv_copy_ms": 12},\n  "batching": {"max_tokens": 1024, "preferred_batch_size": 4}\n}
```

eva: two quick asks: 1) how does batching interact with the FP8 kernel choice? since FP8 microkernels have different vector widths, sometimes bigger batches flip the kernel-selection heuristics. did you run batch>1? 2) can we see calibration prompts used?

raj: good call. I did B=1 mainly to isolate kernel perf. ran a small sweep at B=4 on Mistral-7B — FP8 still wins but the margin shrank (~8-12% improvement vs 25-40% B=1). That aligns with our kernel packing inefficiencies for FP8 at small matrix sizes. calibration set attached (short completion prompts + instruction-like queries).

perf-bot: attached artifacts: /shared/quant_profiles/2026-03-17/adaptive-sweep/ (contains per-model calib logs, kernel traces, kv-copy histograms).

anya: for Qwen-7B the PPL delta looks scary for long-context. Any chance that's calibration mismatch (we used short prompts for calib)?

raj: yep — Qwen's longer context sensitivity is real. When I recalibrated using longer prompts (seq=1024/2048) the fp8_error_estimate dropped from 0.18 -> 0.09 and the routing no longer demoted as often. So calibration prompt distribution matters a lot.

simon: suggestion: make per-model default cal profiles, and require `calib_context_sample` in profile metadata. then routing uses the profile's context-aware estimator. saves us from ad-hoc mismatches.

michael: also worth adding a cheap on-request probe: run a 5-token probe on the selected kernel and compute a quick micro-PPL; if probe error > X then fallback immediately. low overhead and prevents long outputs at bad quality.

raj: agreed. I'll prototype the probe + context-aware profile fields. plan: 1) add `calib_context_sample` to model profiles 2) add probe step before heavy outputs 3) tune fallbacks separately per model class.

eva: can you add a note about the observed kv-copy penalty per device type? ops needs that for Dedicated capacity sizing.

raj: noted — quick summary: A100: warm-kv copy 3-6ms, H100: 2-4ms, T4/V100: 7-12ms. Qwen larger hidden dims push the higher end. I'll dump a csv to the artifacts.

anya: thanks — one last thing, please add the routing config to `profiles/shared` with model-specific overrides so teams can reuse. maybe prefix with `adaptive-quant-v1` and mark it experimental.

raj: will do. I'll upload `adaptive-quant-v1.json` to /profiles/shared/ and ping this thread. planning to run a cluster canary next Tue. :rocket:

michael: when you flip canary, please include these three tests: long-chat (seq=3k), instruction-short (seq<128), and multi-turn prefix reuse — that last one catches kv reuse regressions.

raj: added to test plan. thanks all.

perf-bot: note: audit log created at /audit/quant-routing/1865007890.json

simon: awesome work. low-key: we should add a short doc in docs/perf on "how to pick calibration prompts" — sparks too many silent regressions otherwise.

raj: yup — adding a quick doc next.

(ends)
